server.instructions: Make and edit music in a live FL Studio session: use the run tool (Python with the fl SDK); its description is the manual.

trial.run_description:
Run Python in a persistent kernel, like a notebook cell; variables and imports persist between calls.
The working directory is your workspace, the only place your code can write; files there last for the session.
open(), subprocess, `!cmd` and `%pip install` work, and the internet is reachable.
Pre-bound: fl, theory, Note, AutomationPoint, display; a trailing expression is shown.
Installed: numpy, scipy, soundfile, librosa, matplotlib, pyloudnorm, mido, music21, Pillow.

Returns {outcome, stdout, result | traceback, actions, images}.
outcome is ok, error, interrupted (the call reached its 600 s limit and stopped; variables are kept) or kernel_lost (variables gone, files kept).
Images show as in a notebook: end with a figure or PIL image, call display(...), or leave figures open; at most 4 per call.
actions lists what FL did, one sentence per change, even when the cell failed.
Time in fl calls counts toward the limit: a cell stops between fl calls, and an fl call that cannot finish in the time left, such as a long render, is refused before it starts, so split long work across calls.

Good to know:
- print(fl.scene()) shows the whole project in one digest: patterns, channels, playlist and mixer.
- You hear by measuring: fl.meters() takes seconds, a render plays in real time.

fl: The live FL Studio session: every call applies to FL at once and returns the result, or raises with the reason. Notes, playlist clips, automation clips and the project's notes are read from the song FL opened plus the edits made through fl, so changes to them in FL's own windows are not seen until FL saves the song, which a trial FL cannot do; everything else is read from FL live. A channel is its index, exact name or a unique part of its name. help(fl.render) gives a member's arguments, defaults, results and limits.
  Read     scene(...) tempo channels mixer playlist patterns
  Notes    track(name_or_index, ...) track.write(notes, ...) track.notes() track.clear() Note(key, start, length, ...) theory.chord(root, ...) theory.scale(root, ...) theory.drums(pattern, ...) theory.transpose(notes, semitones) theory.quantize(notes, ...)
  Sound    sounds(...) audition(preset, ...) load_sample(channel, sample) separate(audio, ...) load_preset(channel, preset) presets(channel) set_preset(channel, preset) track.params(...) track.set_param(param, value)
  Mix      track.set_levels(...) route(channel, mixer_track) send(src_track, dst_track, ...) effect(mixer_track, slot) effect.params(...) effect.set_param(param, value)
  Song     set_tempo(bpm) new_pattern(name, ...) rename_pattern(pattern, name) place(pattern, bars) automate(points, bar, ...)
  Hear     meters(...) render(output, ...) read_wav(path)
  Project  undo()
  Guides   guide(...)

Guides: optional reference on techniques and how this environment works, each with a worked example; fl.guide("arrangement") prints one:
  arrangement  How patterns, the playlist and automation work through fl.
  chops        Editing a sample in Python and playing it on a channel.
  listening    Measuring a render, since playback cannot be heard.
  mixing       How levels, panning, sends and effects are set from code.
  sidechain    Ducking one part under another, such as the kick, with drawn automation.
  sounds       Finding sounds by how they sound, hearing them and loading them.

workspace_only.instructions: A Python workspace with no FL Studio session: use the run tool; its description says what it has.
